{"version":3,"name":"Travel writing","description":"Prose about going somewhere, built out of the trip and what the writer noticed on it. It runs from pilgrimage and Grand Tour accounts to the reported travel book and the modern dispatch. Description, encounter, and whatever the writer knows or has looked up about the place are mixed together. Writers in it often end up writing about themselves.","provenance":{"basis":"cited"},"maps":[{"map":"writing","explanation":"The Library of Congress files it under creative nonfiction, and the tradition runs from pilgrimage accounts to the modern travel book.","sourceIds":["lcgft-travel-writing","wp-travel-literature"]}],"broader":[{"cellId":"creative-nonfiction","explanation":"The Library of Congress files Travel writing under Creative nonfiction.","sourceIds":["lcgft-travel-writing"]}],"relations":[],"questions":["Dana and Slocum have moved to the Outdoor literature leaf and the Ship's log record to Logbooks. Twain stays here: no citable name was found for comic travel writing, so the leaf that record needs does not exist yet."],"sources":[{"id":"lcgft-travel-writing","title":"Travel writing — Library of Congress Genre/Form Terms","url":"https://id.loc.gov/authorities/genreForms/gf2014026200"},{"id":"wp-travel-literature","title":"Travel literature — Wikipedia","url":"https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Travel_literature"}],"manifestations":[{"entitySet":"WritingStyles","entityId":"en-019f2eed-2c97-7891-bb08-2e586e7b9e89","explanation":"The record's credits name \"American travel-humor tradition\" (UnderReview). It is built from The Innocents Abroad (1869), a travel book.","sourceIds":["wp-travel-literature"]}],"studies":[]}

{"version":3,"name":"Triolets","description":"Eight-line poems on two rhymes in which the first line returns as the fourth and the first two lines return as the last two. The form is medieval French and was revived in English in the nineteenth century, mostly for light verse. Five of its eight lines are repetition, so almost everything depends on how the returns fall.","provenance":{"basis":"cited"},"maps":[{"map":"writing","explanation":"A named fixed form with a stated repetition rule, a medieval origin and a documented revival; LCGFT files it directly under Poetry.","sourceIds":["lcgft-triolets","wp-triolet"]}],"broader":[{"cellId":"poetry","explanation":"Its Library of Congress record gives Poetry as a broader term.","sourceIds":["lcgft-triolets"]}],"relations":[],"questions":[],"sources":[{"id":"lcgft-triolets","title":"Triolets — Library of Congress Genre/Form Terms","url":"https://id.loc.gov/authorities/genreForms/gf2014026578"},{"id":"wp-triolet","title":"Triolet — Wikipedia","url":"https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Triolet"}],"manifestations":[],"studies":[]}

{"version":3,"name":"Trompe-l'oeil painting","description":"Painting that describes objects at actual size and in the viewer's own light so that they read as physically present. It works with shallow depth, hard edges, cast shadow and materials that lie flat against a surface, and its stock subjects are pinned papers, letter racks, niches and cupboard shelves.","provenance":{"basis":"cited"},"maps":[{"map":"art","explanation":"A pictorial tradition with a long and documented body of work.","sourceIds":["wp-trompe-loeil","aat-trompe-loeil"]}],"broader":[],"relations":[],"questions":[],"sources":[{"id":"wp-trompe-loeil","title":"Trompe-l'œil — Wikipedia","url":"https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trompe-l%27%C5%93il"},{"id":"aat-trompe-loeil","title":"trompe-l'oeil — Getty AAT 300056506","url":"https://vocab.getty.edu/aat/300056506"}],"manifestations":[{"entitySet":"ArtStyles","entityId":"en-01a068cf-50b6-7622-bcf6-8f7f34974f89","explanation":"The record's credits name \"Trompe-l'oeil painting\" (UnderReview).","sourceIds":["wp-trompe-loeil"]},{"entitySet":"ArtStyles","entityId":"en-01a068ca-d8ed-71f0-9cd3-d588a253af9b","explanation":"The record's credits name \"Trompe-l'oeil painting\" (UnderReview).","sourceIds":["wp-trompe-loeil"]},{"entitySet":"ArtStyles","entityId":"en-01a068cf-e9cc-7bf3-b567-c293e550e410","explanation":"The record's credits name \"Trompe-l'oeil painting\" (UnderReview).","sourceIds":["wp-trompe-loeil"]},{"entitySet":"DesignLanguages","entityId":"en-01a068ca-dab5-7080-a495-a616e07eba77","explanation":"The record's credits name \"Trompe-l'oeil painting\" (Published).","sourceIds":["wp-trompe-loeil"]},{"entitySet":"DesignLanguages","entityId":"en-01a068cf-52f7-7bf1-9dde-2c82011c3585","explanation":"The record's credits name \"Trompe-l'oeil painting\" (Published).","sourceIds":["wp-trompe-loeil"]},{"entitySet":"DesignLanguages","entityId":"en-01a068cf-ebd9-7ad3-942d-09172ab69209","explanation":"The record's credits name \"Trompe-l'oeil painting\" (Published).","sourceIds":["wp-trompe-loeil"]}],"studies":[]}

{"version":3,"name":"Tweetstorm","description":"An essay published as a numbered run of short posts, built so that a post reads alone and pulls the reader to the next. It became popular from around 2016, when writers began posting essays in real time as sequences of tweets capped at 140 and later 280 characters. The craft advice is consistent. Number from the first post, put one move in each, write the sequence before posting it, and give every post something a reader would stop for. {"version":3,"name":"Vampire fiction","description":"Fiction about the undead who feed on the living, a tradition with its own worked-out rules about thresholds, daylight and consent. {"version":3,"name":"Viennese Actionism","description":"A short-lived Austrian movement of the 1960s and early 1970s in which Nitsch, Brus, Mühl and Schwarzkogler staged violent ritual actions using blood, animal carcasses and their own bodies. {"version":3,"name":"Villancicos (Poetry)","description":"Iberian and Latin American poems of the late fifteenth to eighteenth centuries, built on a refrain with stanzas that return to it, written to be sung. The refrain structure is what the name names.","provenance":{"basis":"cited"},"maps":[{"map":"writing","explanation":"A named poetic and musical form with a stated refrain structure, a defined period and identified authors; LCGFT files it directly under Poetry.","sourceIds":["lcgft-villancicos-poetry","wp-villancico"]}],"broader":[{"cellId":"poetry","explanation":"Its Library of Congress record gives Poetry as a broader term.","sourceIds":["lcgft-villancicos-poetry"]}],"relations":[],"questions":[],"sources":[{"id":"lcgft-villancicos-poetry","title":"Villancicos (Poetry) — Library of Congress Genre/Form Terms","url":"https://id.loc.gov/authorities/genreForms/gf2014026586"},{"id":"wp-villancico","title":"Villancico — Wikipedia","url":"https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Villancico"}],"manifestations":[],"studies":[]}

{"version":3,"name":"Villanelle","description":"Nineteen lines in five tercets and a quatrain, on two rhymes, with the first and third lines returning alternately as refrains and together at the end. The fixed form is a nineteenth-century French codification of a looser Italian song; Thomas's Do not go gentle and Bishop's One Art are the best-known English instances. The refrains change meaning by being repeated.","provenance":{"basis":"cited"},"maps":[{"map":"writing","explanation":"A named fixed form with a stated refrain rule, a documented codification and a modern canon; LCGFT files it directly under Poetry.","sourceIds":["lcgft-villanelle","wp-villanelle"]}],"broader":[{"cellId":"poetry","explanation":"Its Library of Congress record gives Poetry as a broader term.","sourceIds":["lcgft-villanelle"]}],"relations":[],"questions":[],"sources":[{"id":"lcgft-villanelle","title":"Villanelle — Library of Congress Genre/Form Terms","url":"https://id.loc.gov/authorities/genreForms/gf2014026587"},{"id":"wp-villanelle","title":"Villanelle — Wikipedia","url":"https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Villanelle"}],"manifestations":[],"studies":[]}

{"version":3,"name":"Weird fiction","description":"Horror that drops the inherited monsters and invents things that fit no category, aiming at awe as much as fear. It formed in the late nineteenth and early twentieth centuries around Hodgson, M. R. James, Clark Ashton Smith and Lovecraft. The writing works by withholding, by the narrator's failure to describe, and by a scale that makes the human observer irrelevant. Its recurring move is a document or a report presented as evidence.","provenance":{"basis":"cited"},"maps":[{"map":"writing","explanation":"A subgenre with a fixed period, a canon and a critical literature.","sourceIds":["wp-weird-fiction"]}],"broader":[{"cellId":"horror-fiction","explanation":"It works inside supernatural horror and either avoids or reinterprets that tradition's antagonists.","sourceIds":["wp-weird-fiction"]}],"relations":[{"cellId":"gothic-fiction","label":"reacted against","explanation":"It invents its monsters instead of using the Gothic stock of ghosts, vampires and werewolves.","sourceIds":["wp-weird-fiction"]}],"questions":[],"sources":[{"id":"wp-weird-fiction","title":"Weird fiction — Wikipedia","url":"https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Weird_fiction"}],"manifestations":[],"studies":[]}

{"version":3,"name":"Wellington Group","description":"A group of New Zealand poets working in and around Wellington in the 1950s and 1960s, associated with Louis Johnson's New Zealand Poetry Yearbook. They quarrelled with Allen Curnow over his anthologising, and the exchange is on the record.","provenance":{"basis":"cited"},"maps":[{"map":"writing","explanation":"A named literary movement with a period, identified members and a body of work. {"version":3,"name":"Western fiction","description":"Fiction of the American frontier in the decades of westward expansion, with the conflict between law and lawlessness as its recurring shape. Its conventions are strong enough that revisionist Westerns are read as arguments with them.","provenance":{"basis":"cited"},"maps":[{"map":"writing","explanation":"A genre with conventions firm enough to be argued against from inside, a dated history and a large canon; LCGFT files it directly under Fiction.","sourceIds":["lcgft-western-fiction","wp-western-fiction"]}],"broader":[{"cellId":"fiction","explanation":"Its Library of Congress record gives Fiction as a broader term.","sourceIds":["lcgft-western-fiction"]}],"relations":[],"questions":["Borderline against the rule that declined Campus fiction and Railroad fiction as setting-defined. {"version":3,"name":"Wiener Gruppe","description":"A small Austrian avant-garde constellation formed around H. C. {"version":3,"name":"Wordless novels","description":"Book-length narratives told entirely in sequences of captionless pictures, one image to a page. {"version":3,"name":"Yakṣagāna plays","description":"Dance drama from coastal Karnataka staging episodes from the Mahabharata, the Ramayana and the Puranas through the night, with heavy make-up, towering headgear and a singer who narrates while the actors improvise dialogue. {"version":3,"name":"Young British Artists","description":"A loose London group first exhibiting together in 1988, many of them from the Goldsmiths fine art course, who used shock, entrepreneurship and self-organised shows to reach an audience quickly.
